- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline at 5% below peak or adjust to mean of prior 5-day range.  
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.  
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), sentiment is often bearish — increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect potential reversal.  
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3 consecutive days below 70), reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect trend correction.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust — apply a 2–5% downward correction to forecast.
